items.title: 52263_Sonny Greer oral history interview
items.q: I recorded with Jelly for Clarence Williams.

ctx.x: No. Never recorded. Pathetic, they never recorded that guy. You know, it was hard unless you was in the circle. Clarence Williams had the recording things locked up. He wasn't in there, wasn't nothing happening, you know what I mean? He didn't have no reputation because didn't nobody know him. He's from some little old town over here in Jersey. Didn't nobody know who the hell he was. Pathetic, man. I wish they
could have got him. He was something else, though. I don't know whether he's living. I guess --

items.title: 52263_Sonny Greer oral history interview
items.q: In Clarence William's office. I was so busy, I didn't know anybody by the name of Jelly Roll.

ctx.x: Must have been in the mid-twenties?

Whether it was in New York or on the Coast. I think it was in New York. In Clarence William's office. I was so busy, I didn't know anybody by the name of Jelly Roll. I wasn't that deeply involved that this guy is that and this guy -- it wasn't like that amongst the colored musicians. It wasn't like that. They say, "Hey, Sonny, meet so and so." Okay, "Daddy, how are you? Fine, good knowing you."
Well, he wasn't outstanding with a great big spotlight in front of them's back then. Like them singers, them big singers. We just --
